subject.title: fix(codex): restore native PreToolUse relay delivery

question: After the Code Mode policy normalization blocker is fixed, should OpenClaw accept policy-active Codex sessions being routed through unified exec and starting fresh when native hook relay config fingerprints drift?
rationale: The code defect is mechanically repairable, but the remaining behavior changes tool-execution routing and persisted Codex thread continuity for existing policy-active users; that security and upgrade tradeoff needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Fix Normalization, Then Review Tradeoff
options.body: Repair the Code Mode policy-surface gap first, then have maintainers explicitly accept or reject the unified-exec and fresh-thread behavior before merge.

options.title: Pause Until Packaged Codex Proof
options.body: Keep the draft paused until the bundled `@openai/codex` package version is proven to emit the required native PreToolUse events without a local patch.

options.title: Choose A Broader Fail-Closed Strategy
options.body: If maintainers do not want to rely on positive native hook delivery, supersede this branch with an explicit fail-closed or native-surface-disable strategy.

recommendation.title: Fix Normalization, Then Review Tradeoff
recommendation.body: Repair the Code Mode policy-surface gap first, then have maintainers explicitly accept or reject the unified-exec and fresh-thread behavior before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work and prior merge history on Code Mode hook contracts and native relay fallback make this the best available owner for the security/compatibility decision.
